# Seikōkan Dojo (誠光館)

> Traditional Toyama-ryu (戸山流) swordsmanship dojo in Casselberry, Florida, led by head instructor Roger Browning.

Seikōkan preserves the practical, combat-derived techniques of Toyama-ryu battojutsu while emphasizing the character-building principles of Budō: discipline, respect, and personal growth through the way of the sword.

## About

- School name: Seikōkan (誠光館), meaning roughly "Hall of Sincere Light"
- Style: Toyama-ryu (戸山流) Battojutsu, a practical Japanese sword school with roots in military training
- Location: Casselberry, Florida, USA
- Training schedule: Sundays, 10:00–11:30 AM
- Head instructor: Roger Browning — 5th Dan, All Japan Toyama-ryu Iaido Federation; also holds rank in Tamiya-ryu, Chito-ryu Karate, and San Bao Pai Kung Fu

## Training programs

- Kihon (Foundation): sword etiquette, drawing, stances, sheathing, fundamental cutting
- Kata & Tameshigiri: classical forms and test-cutting practice on rolled straw targets (wara)
- Kumitachi: partner practice with wooden (bokken) and blunted metal (mogitō) swords
- Advanced Applications: combat interpretation, advanced tameshigiri, teaching methodology

## Philosophy

Three core principles guide the dojo's practice:
- Makoto (誠, sincerity) — honest self-reflection and persistent effort
- Tanren (鍛錬, forging) — disciplined repetition that refines both technique and spirit
- Tamashii (魂, spirit) — an indomitable spirit cultivated through dedicated practice
